title: Hatchet

cover.description: Cover of the Simon and Schuster trade paperback edition.
cover.alt: Book cover showing a light silhouette of a hatchet in front of a woodland scene.  Text over the image says 'HATCHET / GARY PAULSEN / Three-time Newbery Honor author

overview: A 13-year old boy on the way to visit his father has to land a plane after its pilot suffers a heart attack, and then must learn to survive on his own in the Canadian wilderness with little more than a hatchet, a gun, and a few other items he salvages from the plane. Gary Paulsen's novel won Newbery honors in 1988, and has remained a best-seller for young readers in the decades since it was first published.

incidents.description: Hatchet was one of {ln:https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_IOOUZHvYbBnngH85zeM07bwav_T83hi/preview|over 2000 books} that Texas Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick {ln:https://www.khou.com/article/news/local/full-list-books-dan-patrick-school-libraries/285-dccb696d-e6d8-4a6b-88e1-c1e06e4c800a|called for school libraries to remove from their shelves}, or have their school district penalized in state accountability ratings if they fail to do so.  Writing for the Texas Observer, librarian Kalyn Gensic calls Patrick's threat {ln:https://www.texasobserver.org/dan-patrick-books-come-and-take-them/|'a hostage situation taking shape.'}  As she puts it, 'Take this list that was formed outside of your community, outside of the purview of the parents you serve... and just remove the books. It’s so simple. And if you don’t, we’ll break your school. We’ll punish your whole community.'
